sources.title: Baridshahi Dynasty, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Authoritative chronology, political identity, Qasim Barid, Ali Barid, Talikota, cultural achievements, decline, and annexation.

sources.title: Mahmud Gawan: Deccanis and Westerners, Cambridge University Press
sources.note: Scholarly chapter on Bidar as a Bahmani capital, its transregional networks, court, and institutional inheritance.

sources.title: Deccan: Political and literary history, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Regional political history of the Bahmani successor states, their alliances, conflicts, literature, and conquests.

sources.title: Deccan: Architecture and art, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Scholarly survey of Bidar buildings, craftsmen, tiles, Persian connections, and Deccani artistic development.

sources.title: The Sultanates of the Deccan, Cambridge History of Islam
sources.note: Authoritative synthesis of sixteenth-century Deccan politics, alliances, Talikota, encroachment, and annexation.

sources.title: Deccan Sultanates, SOAS Research Online
sources.note: Scholarly overview placing Bidar among the distinct, short-lived Deccan successor sultanates.

sources.title: Dynastic History of the Deccan, Maharashtra State Gazetteers
sources.note: Government historical synthesis with a dedicated Barid Shahi narrative and regional chronology.

sources.title: Indo-Islamic Architecture, Archaeological Survey of India
sources.note: Archaeological Survey overview of Deccan architecture, including the Barid Shahi tomb tradition and Ali Barid tomb.

sources.title: Bidar: Its History and Monuments, Ghulam Yazdani
sources.note: Foundational archaeological monograph documenting Bidar buildings, inscriptions, waterworks, chronology, and layered patronage.

sources.title: Barid Shahi Tombs, Archaeological Survey of India Dharwad Circle
sources.note: Official monument record for the Barid Shahi royal tomb complex at Bidar.

sources.title: Historical Monuments, Bidar District Government
sources.note: Government description of fort planning, palaces, kitchen, bath, cistern, harem rooms, tombs, and layered architecture.

sources.title: District Census Handbook Bidar, Census of India
sources.note: Official district handbook summarizing Bidar geography, history, fort, monuments, settlements, and regional setting.

sources.title: Mahmud Gawan Madrasa, Incredible India
sources.note: Government tourism record describing the inherited madrasa, library, lecture halls, rooms, curriculum, and later damage.

sources.title: History of India 650 to 1526, Pondicherry University
sources.note: University study material on Mahmud Gawan Madrasa architecture, library, teaching halls, and residential arrangements.

sources.title: The Courts of the Deccan Sultanates, Cambridge University Press
sources.note: Scholarly synthesis of diverse courtly society, transregional networks, knowledge, bodily practice, and learned skills.

sources.title: Courtly Disposition, The Courts of the Deccan Sultanates
sources.note: Scholarly chapter on education, diet, medicine, physicians, hospitals, perfumes, sociability, and bodily knowledge.

sources.title: Courts, Merchants and Commodities, The Courts of the Deccan Sultanates
sources.note: Scholarly chapter on Deccan trade, revenue, merchants, commodities, consumption, and courtly exchange.

sources.title: A Social History of the Deccan, 1300 to 1761
sources.note: Authoritative social history emphasizing mobility, piety, labor, language, regional identities, and individual lives.

sources.title: Rama Raya: Elite mobility in a Persianized world
sources.note: Scholarly chapter documenting mobile, multilingual Deccan elites and connections involving Bidar before Talikota.

sources.title: Rehabilitation of the Qanat and Karez system of Bidar, Deccan Heritage Foundation
sources.note: Conservation documentation for the fifteenth-century underground water system, geology, distribution, and continued use.

sources.title: Water in Hyderabad and the Deccan, Oxford Academic
sources.note: Scholarly regional framework for water as an environmental, technical, social, and political resource in the Deccan.

sources.title: Bidri ware, Scientific Analysis of Ancient and Historic Metals
sources.note: Scientific account of high-zinc alloy, blackening, inlay, earliest surviving objects, and unresolved origins.

sources.title: Bidriware: history, technique and conservation
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of Bidri alloy, casting, engraving, inlay, blackening, soil traditions, and debated origins.

sources.title: Enigmas of bidri, Studies in Conservation
sources.note: Peer-reviewed technical discussion of Bidri composition, manufacture, corrosion, conservation, and unresolved questions.

sources.title: Learning through objects: Bidriware in the SOAS Collections
sources.note: University collection account of craft stages, teaching objects, uncertain origins, products, and movement among centers.

sources.title: Annual Report of the Archaeological Department of Hyderabad State
sources.note: Official archaeological report on Barid Shahi history, coin evidence, inscriptions, monuments, chronology, and dynastic limits.

sources.title: Traditions and Perceptions of Crafts in Bharat, IGNOU
sources.note: University teaching resource placing Bidri within Indian craft traditions and skilled production.

sources.title: Epigraphia Indica, Arabic and Persian Supplement 1937 to 1938
sources.note: Archaeological epigraphy publication containing five Bidar inscriptions, original texts, translations, dates, and contexts.

sources.title: Ancient India Number 5, Archaeological Survey of India
sources.note: Archaeological Survey report on the bilingual Persian and Marathi Ashtur well inscriptions and Barid court context.

sources.title: Sultans of Deccan India 1500 to 1700, Metropolitan Museum of Art
sources.note: Museum scholarship on Deccani architecture, manuscripts, metalwork, Bidri production, materials, and artistic exchange.

sources.title: Bidri Box for Holding Pan, Metropolitan Museum of Art
sources.note: Museum record for a Bidar-attributed zinc-alloy box, silver and brass inlay, architecture-inspired form, and pan use.

sources.title: Bidri ware flask, British Museum
sources.note: Museum object record explaining blackened zinc-rich Bidri alloy, silver and brass inlay, form, and Deccan attribution.

proposedOverrides.name: Bidar Sultanate (Barid Shahi dynasty)
